Liverpool's left-back, Andy Robertson, emphasized the critical role of solidifying the team's defense as a cornerstone for a potential title contention under their new manager, Arne Slot. Robertson highlighted the encouraging start with two consecutive clean sheets in their initial matches, recognizing the upcoming challenge posed by Manchester United at Old Trafford, where the defense is anticipated to face a far sterner examination. The recent shutouts against Ipswich and Brentford demonstrated the team's defensive resolve, providing Slot with an ideal beginning. Last season, Liverpool's defensive record saw them conceding 41 goals throughout the campaign, ultimately placing them third, a notable seven goals more than Manchester City and twelve goals more than Arsenal, highlighting their defensive vulnerabilities in comparison to the title-winning and runner-up teams. Robertson's comments shed light on the team's ambition to minimize conceding opportunities as a crucial element in their pursuit of silverware. He pointed out that the team's inability to keep clean sheets came back to haunt them.

To handle the upcoming Manchester United encounter is a significant test for the team's defensive resilience. Robertson stressed the importance of maintaining a tight defensive structure, aiming to restrict the opposition's goal-scoring opportunities. This focus on defensive stability extends beyond the Manchester United game. Robertson underlined the team's dedication to continue this trend throughout the season, striving to limit chances for every opponent they face after there is a break for international games. He has noticed that the teams have a better defense than them. This commitment is deeply rooted in the recognition that defensive lapses can severely disrupt title aspirations. Robertson made reference to the previous season's statistics, noting that Liverpool, even when still in contention for the title, were allowing a greater number of opportunities to opponents than their rivals, Arsenal and Manchester City. This defensive fragility, he explained, proved to be costly, as inevitable games arose where they were punished for their vulnerabilities.

Robertson's analysis underscored the significance of establishing a reliable defensive foundation as a prerequisite for mounting a serious title challenge. The improvement in their collective defending is a must. The team needs to make many defensive changes. The early signs of improvement under Arne Slot, with the back-to-back clean sheets, provide a promising foundation. However, Robertson recognizes that the true measure of their progress will be revealed in demanding fixtures against formidable opponents like Manchester United. The team's ambition is clear: to transform their defense into a formidable shield, minimizing chances and maximizing their chances of securing a title under their new manager. This defensive resilience, coupled with their attacking prowess, will be pivotal in determining Liverpool's success in the upcoming season.

P.S. The Guardian article emphasizes the importance of Liverpool's defense and it must improve to seriously challenge for the title under Arne Slot. Andy Robertson highlights the team's need to improve both individually and collectively their defensive skills in order both the team and the club can succeed. The two clean sheets in the opening games are encouraging, but the upcoming game against Manchester United will be a true test. The team has a chance to improve.
